'''Robert H. Brandenberger''' (born 1956) is a [[Swiss Canadians|Swiss-Canadian]] theoretical [[cosmologist]] and a professor of [[physics]] at [[McGill University]] in Montreal, [[Quebec]], [[Canada]].

==Biography==
Brandenberger completed his undergraduate degree at [[ETH Zurich]], in Switzerland, and went on to receive his Ph.D. from [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=74906}}</ref> He was a postdoctoral student under [[Stephen Hawking]] at the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge#Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics|Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] (DAMTP) at the University of Cambridge.<ref>[https://www.thestar.com/news/world/2018/03/14/stephen-hawking-helped-elevate-canadas-profile-in-physics-community.html Stephen Hawking helped elevate Canada’s profile in physics community]. ''The Star''. Peter Goffin. The Canadian Press. March 14, 2018. </ref> He also did postdoctoral work at the Institute for [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]], [[University of California]], [[Santa Barbara, California|Santa Barbara]]. Professor Brandenberger joined the faculty of [[Brown University]] in 1987 and then in 2004, he joined McGill University where he is a Canada Research Chair (Tier 1) holder.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=1553|title=Canada Research Chairs|first=Industry Canada|last=Government of Canada|date=November 29, 2012|website=www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca}}</ref> He is also an affiliate member of the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/people/Robert-Brandenberger|title=Robert Brandenberger &#124; Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca}}</ref>  

With [[Cumrun Vafa]], Brandenberger developed [[Inflation (cosmology)#String gas cosmology|string gas cosmology]]. In particular, they proposed the [[Brandenberger–Vafa mechanism]] as an alternative to [[inflationary cosmology]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brandenberger |first=Robert |last2=Vafa |first2=Cumrun |date=April 10, 1989 |title=Superstrings in the Early Universe |journal=[[Nuclear Physics B]] |volume=2 |pages=391–410 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(89)90037-}}</ref> Because the original model did not address the questions of entropy and [[Flatness problem|flatness]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brandenberger |first1=Robert H. |last2=Nayeri |first2=ALI |last3=Patil |first3=Subodh P. |last4=Vafa |first4=Cumrun |date=2007 |title=String Gas Cosmology and Structure Formation |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/978863 |journal=[[International Journal of Modern Physics A]] |volume=22 |issue=21 |pages=3621–3642 |arxiv=hep-th/0608121 |bibcode=2007IJMPA..22.3621B |doi=10.1142/S0217751X07037159 |s2cid=5899352}}</ref> Brandenberger and his colleagues have been working on improving it.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lashkari |first1=Nima |last2=Brandenberger |first2=Robert H |date=September 17, 2008 |title=Speed of sound in string gas cosmology |journal=[[Journal of High Energy Physics]] |volume=2008 |issue=9 |page=082 |arxiv=0806.4358 |bibcode=2008JHEP...09..082L |doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2008/09/082 |issn=1029-8479 |s2cid=119184258}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Kamali |first1=Vahid |last2=Brandenberger |first2=Robert |date=May 11, 2020 |title=Creating spatial flatness by combining string gas cosmology and power law inflation |journal=[[Physical Review D]] |language=en |volume=101 |issue=10 |article-number=103512 |arxiv=2002.09771 |bibcode=2020PhRvD.101j3512K |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.101.103512 |issn=2470-0010 |doi-access=free}}</ref> During the 2000s, when the [[Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe]] (WMAP) was in operation observing the [[cosmic microwave background]], a number of theorists, including Hawking and Alan Guth, the founder of the theory of cosmic inflation, explored the implications of [[Brane|p-branes]], which are hypothetical objects in [[string theory]], for cosmology. With Natalia Shuhmaher, Brandenberger constructed a model of a brane gas to explain why the observed universe has only three dimensions.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brandenberger |first=Robert |last2=Shuhmaher |first2=Natalia |date=April 24, 2006 |title=Brane Gas-Driven Bulk Expansion as a Precursor Stage to Brane Inflation |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.161301 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=96 |article-number=161301 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.161301}}</ref><ref name=":52">{{Cite book |last=Ferguson |first=Kitty |author-link=Kitty Ferguson |title=Stephen Hawking: An Unfettered Mind |publisher=Palgrave MacMillan |year=2012 |isbn=978-0-230-34060-2}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=225}}  

==Honors and awards==
He has won numerous awards for his work, including the [[Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1988,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dartmouth.edu/~eejust/symposium/speakers/index.html |title=E. E. Just Program &#124; Home |publisher=Dartmouth.edu |date= |accessdate=2021-02-11}}</ref> the Outstanding Junior Researcher award from the Department of Energy in 1988,<ref name="brown">{{cite web|url=https://vivo.brown.edu/?id=1106970239|title=Researchers @ Brown|website=vivo.brown.edu}}</ref> the Killam Research Fellowship in 2009,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mcgill.ca/channels/news/mcgill-physicist-awarded-killam-research-fellowship-105401|title=McGill physicist awarded Killam Research Fellowship|first=Contact Information Contact: Allison Flynn Organization: Media Relations Office Email: allison j flynnmcgill ca Office|last=Phone: 514-398-7698|website=Channels}}</ref> and the [[CAP-CRM Prize in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cap.ca/medal/publicity/press.php?year=2011&medal_id=6 |title=CAP Medal Press Release - 2011 CRM |access-date=2013-03-04 |archive-date=2015-02-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150219051740/http://www.cap.ca/medal/publicity/press.php?year=2011&medal_id=6 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2001 <ref> {{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2001&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|accessdate=17 September 2020}} </ref>
